title: Sample a quadratic permutation prefix using affine radical fibres
statement: On the common polar radical L, the prefix is affine along each coset. Bijectivity gives equal-size feasible core fibres; a core seed and a kernel seed yield exactly uniform prefix-conditioned inputs and exactly n-t fresh bits.

requires: correct acquired quadratic permutation prefix F_t
common polar radical and a complement
provides: compiled affine-core inverse after full acquisition
assumptions: runtime qualification applies simultaneously with correct acquisition, not every erroneous branch
costs: all core enumeration, elimination and seeds paid
contract.obstruction: Avoids hiding a rare-prefix conditional sampler; not an unconditional expected FPT runtime guarantee.

evidence.quote: There is no rare-prefix rejection or hidden conditional sampler.

review.scope: Exact source-supported extraction only; any scoped substantive acceptance is a separate version-bound review overlay.
